tasks.short: Prepare work schedules, coordinate calendars, and arrange appointments.

steps.what: Collect appointment requests, staffing needs, and availability preferences.
Check calendars, absences, room availability, and working hours.
Build a draft work schedule and identify uncovered periods.
Discuss clashes, preferences, and urgent changes with affected people.
Review staffing coverage and approve the work schedule.
Enter and publish the approved work schedule.
Book agreed appointments and send calendar invitations.

tasks.design: Configure request forms and booking rules in {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}, reading availability from {HCM}. A deterministic schedule generator proposes coverage and flags conflicts; manager approval releases the schedule to {HCM}. Routine appointments use delegated booking rules, while disputed changes return to the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive through several channels, and staffing preferences are rarely recorded as usable constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking features handle appointments; AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting availability and building a constrained schedule generator.
tasks.still_hard: Fair allocation, competing priorities, stale availability, and national rules on working time still need local judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk understands which commitments can move and negotiates changes without damaging trust.

ambition.what: Daily coverage-gap decisions before staffing shortages become urgent

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time collecting availability and more time resolving coverage gaps. Within agreed limits, the clerk can select routine alternatives; managers retain staffing approval.

reach.learn: Translate service demand, working-time limits, and essential skills into scheduling constraints.

evidence.claim: Booking rules, availability checks, and constraint scheduling can use configuration and deterministic code; estimates are planning judgements.
In the Netherlands, employee-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent; this does not establish a Europe-wide requirement.

assumptions: The baseline combines calendar screens, an absence register, and a shared scheduling workbook.
Structured intake replaces routine request collection; unusual requests remain with the clerk.
Routine appointment invitations already fall within delegated authority.
The publication gate uses the approval recorded in s5, without a second approval round.
GDPR access controls apply; absence reasons are unnecessary for scheduling.
National rules and employee consultation requirements must be checked before changing scheduling practices.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates; consultation elapsed time can be longer.
unknowns: Whether the {HCM} already provides adequate scheduling features.
Available interfaces, room-booking support, and calendar permissions.
Actual coverage rules, collective agreements, and approval limits.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Can existing configuration generate acceptable schedules before custom code is needed?
Which constraints explain most rejected draft schedules?
Does the intended use require additional controls under the EU AI Act?
new_work: Maintain coverage constraints and delegated booking limits.
Resolve infeasible schedules and incomplete requests.
Check failed synchronisations and prevent duplicate invitations.
Review access permissions and changes to working-time rules.

tasks.short: Turn notes and dictation into accurate, formatted correspondence and documents.

steps.what: Receive notes, dictation, recipient details, and document instructions.
Type source notes or audio-recorder dictation into a first draft.

loop.input: Source notes or dictation recording, with document instructions.
loop.output: Source transcript with uncertain passages and source references.
loop.check: Check source coverage; the clerk verifies uncertain passages, names, dates, amounts, and commitments against the original.
loop.stop: One extraction and one targeted retry; unreadable or uncertain passages return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audio and irregular notes cannot always supply reliable fields through forms or fixed parsing.

steps.what: Apply the correct template, layout, headings, and recipient fields.
Proofread the draft and correct wording, factual errors, and omissions.

loop.input: Formatted draft, checked transcript, source notes, and document instructions.
loop.output: Proposed edits and a source-linked list of possible errors or omissions.
loop.check: Configured spelling checks run first; compare names, dates, and amounts exactly. The clerk reviews meaning and unsupported changes.
loop.stop: One review pass and one revision; unresolved factual questions return to the document owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spelling rules cannot assess whether wording preserves the intended meaning or omits a qualification.

steps.what: Approve the document's meaning, commitments, and final wording.
Send the approved document and retain the issued version.

tasks.design: A form in {WORKFLOW} stores source material in {DOCS}; bounded extraction produces a checked transcript. A deterministic generator applies approved templates, while configured checks and a bounded language review propose corrections. Approval releases the exact document version through {EMAIL} and records it in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates solved layout, but handwritten notes, dictation, and varied wording still required manual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Available transcription and language models can propose text, while deterministic templates and version controls constrain its use.
tasks.still_hard: Poor recordings, ambiguous instructions, multilingual nuance, and statements with legal or financial consequences require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk notices when polished wording changes the author's meaning and knows when to ask for clarification.

ambition.what: Accessible plain-language versions of routine office notices

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking meaning and helping authors clarify instructions. Release authority remains with the document owner; the clerk can prepare accessible versions for approval.

reach.learn: Accessible document structure, template fields, version control, and source-based proofreading.

evidence.claim: Amberscript offers machine transcription and human-checked transcription; its accuracy claims are vendor claims.
CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting template-driven document production.
Research documents invented text in speech recognition, supporting source checks before issuing documents.
The proposed review workflow, time allocations, and build ranges are estimates rather than documented outcomes.

assumptions: Most source material is digital notes; a smaller share is handwriting or recorded dictation.
Directly usable digital text bypasses extraction.
The release gate uses approval from s5 and binds it to the exact version and recipients.
GDPR applies to source material, recordings, retention, and processing arrangements.
Employee consultation and recording requirements depend on national rules.
This document workflow does not make employment decisions; EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual deployment.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates.
unknowns: Actual mix of digital notes, handwriting, and recordings.
Languages, audio quality, and accessibility requirements.
Approved templates, retention periods, and document approval rules.
Permitted processing locations and model access arrangements.
research_questions: Which document types can be generated entirely from structured fields?
Can extraction preserve names, figures, and qualifications on representative source material?
Which errors escape existing proofreading and should receive explicit checks?
new_work: Review uncertain transcription and proposed wording changes.
Maintain templates, terminology, and checking rules.
Handle missing instructions and factual disputes.
Check document rendering, version binding, and failed sends.

tasks.short: Check office supplies and arrange approved purchases of materials and services.

steps.what: Count supplies and inspect their condition in storage areas.
Transfer stock counts into the shared supply register.
Check reorder levels, open orders, approved catalogues, and service requests.
Obtain quotes and compare price, availability, specifications, and service terms.

loop.input: Supplier quotes and the purchase requirement.
loop.output: Comparable quote fields with source references and missing-term flags.
loop.check: Validate arithmetic, currency, tax treatment, quantities, and catalogue identifiers; the clerk checks specifications and service terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per quote; missing or conflicting terms return to the clerk before selection.
loop.why_not_simpler: Non-catalogue service quotes use varied prose and layouts; catalogue purchases bypass the loop.

steps.what: Approve the supplier choice, expenditure, and any nonstandard terms.
Create and send the purchase order to the approved supplier.
Inspect delivered supplies or completed services against the order.
Record receipt or report discrepancies for follow-up.

tasks.design: Capture counts and receipt checks once through {WORKFLOW}, updating stock and receipts in {PROCUREMENT}. Configured reorder rules prepare purchases; a bounded extractor handles non-catalogue quotes and produces a checked comparison. Budget approval releases purchase orders, while discrepancies enter a shared exception queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical stock was disconnected from purchase records, while occasional service quotes required manual comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchasing rules and mobile forms cover routine work; small integrations and bounded quote extraction are cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Physical inspection, uncertain demand, supplier substitutions, and the quality of completed services remain difficult to automate.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk notices unsuitable supplies, poor service, and practical needs that stock records miss.

ambition.what: Weekly reorder-level adjustments for frequently depleted office supplies

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time inspecting quality and preventing shortages, with less copying and order entry. The proposed remit adds reorder-level adjustments within budget-holder limits; supplier commitments retain approval.

reach.task: Investigate stock discrepancies and improve replenishment
reach.learn: Cycle counting, lead-time variation, receipt controls, and reorder-level calculation.

evidence.claim: Purchasing configuration can support reorder proposals, approval limits, purchase orders, and receipts.
Quote extraction is a proposed bounded use; the digest does not document this complete purchasing workflow or its savings.

assumptions: The baseline uses a shared stock workbook alongside {PROCUREMENT}.
Point-of-count capture removes the separate transcription step; physical counting remains.
Receipt capture records the clerk's inspection result rather than inferring successful delivery.
The order-release gate reuses the purchase approval from s5.
GDPR applies to supplier contacts and employee request details; collect only necessary data.
National employee consultation requirements must be checked if work allocation or monitoring changes.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates.
unknowns: Whether stock and mobile receipt functions are already available in {PROCUREMENT}.
Catalogue coverage, order volumes, approval limits, and supplier restrictions.
Who may change reorder levels or accept completed services.
Actual stock accuracy, lead times, and frequency of nonstandard quotes.
research_questions: How much purchasing can bypass quote extraction through approved catalogues?
Which stock discrepancies cause avoidable orders?
Can receipt capture update {PROCUREMENT} without duplicate entry?
new_work: Maintain catalogue mappings, reorder levels, and approval limits.
Review extracted quote terms and handle missing specifications.
Investigate stock discrepancies and supplier exceptions.
Check failed order transmissions and duplicate-order controls.

tasks.short: Relay messages and carry out practical office errands.

steps.what: Receive the request and clarify its purpose, urgency, and handling needs.
Find the recipient, destination, contact details, and access arrangements.
Write an errand list and fit trips around deadlines and other duties.
Walk to a coworker and relay a routine message.
Collect the physical item and check handling instructions.
Travel to the destination, complete the errand, and hand over the item.
Tell the requester the outcome or explain an unsuccessful handover.

tasks.design: Configure a request queue in {WORKFLOW}, using directory data from {HCM} and {DOCS} to populate destinations and group trips. Routine messages go directly through {CHAT} or {EMAIL}; physical errands remain with the clerk. A single completion entry triggers status notices and routes failed handovers for follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were informal, and most effort involved movement and physical handling rather than data processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple forms, directory lookups, and notifications can remove coordination work with little custom development.
tasks.still_hard: Travel, access problems, fragile items, sensitive handovers, and recipients who are unavailable remain physical or interpersonal work.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk adapts on site, handles items carefully, and recognises when a message needs a personal conversation.

ambition.what: A bookable same-site errand round for employees with limited mobility

tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves practical service and physical errands. The clerk gains clearer priorities and fewer status interruptions; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Destination grouping, secure handovers, handling instructions, and exception recording.

evidence.claim: Request queues, directory lookups, and completion notifications can use existing workflow configuration without a model.
Physical handling and travel remain human in this design; the digest documents no replacement for those activities.
In the Netherlands, individual worker-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent.

assumptions: The baseline mixes routine verbal messages with physical errands; the steps are branches, not a sequence every request follows.
Only routine messages suitable for digital delivery move to notifications; sensitive conversations remain personal.
Completion notices require a clerk or recipient confirmation and never infer a successful handover.
The final status entry is included in remaining physical execution time.
The proposed errand round operates within existing capacity and does not guarantee urgent delivery.
GDPR applies to directory and request data; service reporting avoids individual speed rankings.
National consultation requirements must be checked if monitoring or work organisation changes.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates.
unknowns: The actual split between routine messages, sensitive messages, and physical errands.
Site distances, access restrictions, and secure-handover requirements.
Directory accuracy and availability of a shared request queue.
Demand and available capacity for an accessible errand round.
research_questions: Which errands disappear when documents or messages are delivered digitally?
Can grouping trips reduce travel without delaying urgent requests?
What confirmation is sufficient for each type of handover?
new_work: Maintain destinations, service windows, and handling categories.
Triage incomplete requests and failed handovers.
Record completion once and investigate missing confirmations.
Review access to sensitive requests and remove stale directory entries.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving scheduling conflicts, checking document meaning, preventing supply shortages, and handling practical exceptions. Physical service remains substantial; wider spending or staffing authority requires an explicit local delegation.
reach: Administrative services manager: translate service demand into coverage decisions.
Word processor and typist: maintain accessible templates and source-based quality checks.
Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerk: investigate stock discrepancies and replenishment needs.
Mail clerk: organise reliable internal delivery rounds.
role.ambitious_version: A shared office-service desk that coordinates bookings, document preparation, replenishment, and accessible errand rounds, with clear approvals and a human contact for exceptions.
